Content:
You forgot the iPad Air 2. That had some key upgrades. For starters, it introduced the laminated display to the iPad, which not only made the display more immersive, but it massively reduced the iPad’s thickness. It was also the first iPad to have 2gb of RAM and a triple core processor, indicating the start of Apple turning the iPad into a powerful machine. It was also the first iPad to have an 8 megapixel camera, not the iPad Pro as you mentioned in the video. 

You also forgot the iPad 10th gen. While not groundbreaking, it did introduce USB C to the base iPads, made the base iPad’s design into the modern iPad design, and it introduced the landscape oriented facetime camera to the iPad lineup.

Author: @swilson42
Content:
Great recap!  I have been on the iPad train since the beginning and it’s the device I dreamed of my entire youthhood. I carried a laptop on every car and train trip and even had a laptop in a backpack playing MP3s while I mowed the grass before phones grew up to that task. 

The iPad is the perfect device for 80% of my personal tech use, which is consumption of content. The other 20% is communication and the phone is best for that. Apple’s intent to replace a PC never made sense to me. I don’t want my tablet to be a PC. It is an entirely different thing and fills an entirely different need. I get that many are fine with content on their phone and only want to carry one device.  To each their own. But for me, the tablet is the clear winner for content consumption and I very much keep my tablet free of the clutter of a PC or anything work-related besides reading things and taking notes. 

I have always been annoyed at Apple for the price of the mini. Would have been a perfect choice for my kids and some car-mounted projects I did before cars came with infotainment, but with the regular base iPad always being substantially cheaper, I could never make any sense of paying substantially more for less. The mini should have been $100 cheaper than the regular size iPad the entire time. Make it a tad slower, a tad thicker, a tad less storage, and it’s mini for less money… perfect. 

Today there are plenty of tablet options and many of them are great. The best reason to choose one over another is the surrounding ecosystem in my book.
